topic: Examen du Premier Trimestre (First Term Examination)

subUnits.title: 12.1 Section A — Questions Objectives (Answer All 30)
notes: Section A — Objective Questions
Instructions: Answer ALL thirty questions. Recommended time: 45 minutes for Section A.
Section A covers ALL topics from this term:
- Character vocabulary: rusé, poli/impoli, honnête/malhonnête, timide/courageux
- Self-description: être (build/character), avoir (hair), adjective agreement
- Aimer/détester: regular -ER pattern, + infinitive or + noun
- Attitude vocabulary: méchant, horrible, drôle, amusant, souriant
- Appreciation: excellent, fantastique, bon, mauvais; c'est + adjective
- Gratitude: merci, je vous remercie; tu vs. vous
- Opinion: je crois que / je pense que / à mon avis
- Apologies: pardon, excusez-moi, je m'excuse, s'il vous plaît
- Rural life vocabulary and quantity expressions
- Pas de vs. pas beaucoup de; mais for balance
Exam Strategy:
- Read all four options before choosing. Apply grammar rules before looking at options. Eliminate obviously wrong answers first.

quiz.q: What does 'poli(e)' mean?
quiz.explanation: 'Poli(e)' means polite — feminine adds -e: polie.

quiz.q: What is the opposite of 'honnête'?
quiz.explanation: 'Malhonnête' (dishonest) is the opposite of 'honnête' — formed with the 'mal-' prefix.

quiz.q: How would you say 'she is not shy'?
quiz.explanation: Correct negation: 'Elle n'est pas timide' — ne + verb + pas.

quiz.q: A complete self-description typically includes ___.
opts: no particular content; anything at all works equally
quiz.explanation: A complete self-description includes physical build (être), hair (avoir), and character (être).

quiz.q: Does 'rusé' change between masculine and feminine forms?
opts: No, it stays the same, like 'timide'
Yes, but only in speech, not writing
quiz.explanation: 'Rusé' ends in '-é' (not '-e') and DOES change — feminine is 'rusée.'

quiz.q: What is the correct conjugation of 'aimer' for 'nous' (we)?
quiz.explanation: 'Nous aimons' — stem aim- + -ons ending for nous.

quiz.q: Détester can be followed by ___.
opts: only an infinitive, never a noun
only a noun, never an infinitive
quiz.explanation: 'Détester' can be followed by either a noun (je déteste l'orange) or an infinitive (je déteste regarder la télévision).

quiz.q: How would you say 'she is funny'?
quiz.explanation: 'Elle est drôle' — 'drôle' is unchanging, same for both genders.

quiz.q: What does 'fantastique' mean?
quiz.explanation: 'Fantastique' means fantastic — it is UNCHANGING (already ends in '-e').

quiz.q: How would you say 'you are kind' informally to a friend?
quiz.explanation: 'Tu es gentil(le)' — informal 'tu' form used with friends and peers.

quiz.q: Which word follows 'je crois' and 'je pense' before stating the opinion?
quiz.explanation: Both 'je crois' and 'je pense' are followed by 'que' before the opinion: je crois QUE c'est bon.

quiz.q: What does 'je m'excuse' mean?
quiz.explanation: 'Je m'excuse' means I apologise or I'm sorry.

quiz.q: What does 'la chasse' mean?
quiz.explanation: 'La chasse' means hunting — a common rural activity.

quiz.q: What does 'peu de' mean?
quiz.explanation: 'Peu de' means little or few — the 'small measuring cup.'

quiz.q: What does 'pas d'hôpital de standard' mean?
quiz.explanation: 'Pas d'hôpital de standard' means no proper or standard hospital.

quiz.q: What does 'pas beaucoup de voitures' mean?
quiz.explanation: 'Pas beaucoup de voitures' means not many vehicles — a moderate lack.

quiz.q: What does 'beaucoup de fruits et des légumes' mean?
opts: A lot of fruits and vegetables
quiz.explanation: 'Beaucoup de fruits et des légumes' means a lot of fruits and vegetables.

quiz.q: What does 'la souffrance' mean?
quiz.explanation: 'La souffrance' means suffering — the general experience of hardship in rural life.

quiz.q: What is the feminine form of 'intelligent'?
quiz.explanation: 'Intelligent' takes the regular +e rule: intelligente.

quiz.q: How would you say 'he is naughty, but she is funny'?
opts: Il est méchant, et elle est drôle
Il est méchant, mais elle est drôle
quiz.explanation: 'Mais' (but) connects the contrast correctly: 'Il est méchant, mais elle est drôle.'

quiz.q: How would you say 'we hate watching television' (nous)?
quiz.explanation: 'Nous détestons' (correctly conjugated) + 'regarder' (infinitive) — the second verb must stay in the infinitive.

quiz.q: What form of address does 'excusez-moi' use?
opts: Neither; it has no form of address
quiz.explanation: 'Excusez-moi' uses the formal 'vous' form — appropriate for strangers, elders, and formal situations.

quiz.q: What does 'l'air frais' mean?
quiz.explanation: 'L'air frais' means fresh air — one of the genuine advantages of rural life.

quiz.q: Why might abundant food be considered an advantage of rural life?
opts: This has no connection to rural life
Access to fresh, plentiful local produce and meat
Rural areas never produce any food
Food is always scarce in rural areas
quiz.explanation: Rural areas typically have access to fresh, locally grown produce and meat — a genuine advantage.

quiz.q: What is the feminine plural form of 'beau'?
quiz.explanation: 'Beau' is a fully irregular adjective — feminine singular is 'belle,' feminine plural is 'belles.'

quiz.q: How would you say 'I believe that it is a good idea'?
opts: Je crois c'est une bonne idée
Je crois de c'est une bonne idée
Je crois à c'est une bonne idée
Je crois que c'est une bonne idée
quiz.explanation: 'Je crois QUE c'est une bonne idée' — 'que' is required between 'crois' and the opinion.

quiz.q: Which of these adjectives is UNCHANGING between masculine and feminine?
quiz.explanation: 'Sympathique' already ends in '-e' and is UNCHANGING — same form for both genders.

quiz.q: What does 'adroit(e)' mean?
quiz.explanation: 'Adroit(e)' means skilful — the opposite of 'maladroit(e)' (clumsy).

quiz.q: When describing someone else, adjective agreement follows ___.
opts: the gender and number of the person being described
quiz.explanation: Adjective agreement ALWAYS follows the gender and number of the noun/person being described, not the speaker.

quiz.q: What are the TWO questions to ask before writing any French adjective?
opts: Is it a noun, and is it a verb?
Who/what is being described, and is it singular or plural?
What time is it, and who is speaking?
quiz.explanation: Before writing any adjective: (1) Who or what is being described? (2) Is the subject singular or plural? These determine the correct form.

subUnits.title: 12.2 Section B — Questions de Théorie
notes: Section B — Theory / Essay Questions
Instructions: Answer ALL FIVE questions in complete French sentences. Show all your working and reasoning — method marks are awarded even when the final answer has a minor error.
Questions:
1. Traduisez CINQ mots de caractère appris ce trimestre (avec leur forme féminine si elle existe).
2. Conjuguez 'aimer' ET 'détester' au présent avec 'je,' 'nous,' et 'ils/elles.'
3. Traduisez: 'I think that French is interesting. Excuse me, please, where is the school?'
4. Expliquez la différence entre 'pas de' et 'pas beaucoup de,' avec un exemple de chaque.
5. Rédaction: rédigez un paragraphe (5 phrases minimum) décrivant une personne (apparence ET caractère) OU la vie rurale (avantages ET désavantages), en utilisant le vocabulaire de ce trimestre.

weeklyAssessment.question: SECTION B — Theory 1: Traduisez CINQ mots de caractère appris ce trimestre (avec leur forme féminine si elle existe).
weeklyAssessment.markingGuide: 1 mark per correctly translated term with correct feminine form (5 total).

weeklyAssessment.question: SECTION B — Theory 2: Conjuguez 'aimer' ET 'détester' au présent avec 'je,' 'nous,' et 'ils/elles.'
weeklyAssessment.markingGuide: 0.83 marks per correctly conjugated form (6 forms across both verbs, 5 total).

weeklyAssessment.question: SECTION B — Theory 3: Traduisez: 'I think that French is interesting. Excuse me, please, where is the school?'
weeklyAssessment.markingGuide: 2.5 marks each for a correctly translated, correctly structured sentence.

weeklyAssessment.markingGuide: Clear explanation (3); valid examples for both (2).

weeklyAssessment.markingGuide: Five grammatically correct, well-structured sentences covering the chosen topic thoroughly (5, holistic).
